title: G2: Completeness — non-SN(R/S) implies an infinite relative chain

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Direction:** $\neg\mathrm{SN}(R/S)\Rightarrow$ exists infinite relative chain (contrapositive of task (1)'s $\Leftarrow$).

Use the characterization: $\neg\mathrm{SN}(R/S)$ iff there is an infinite $\to_{R\cup S}$ derivation with infinitely many $\to_R$-steps. Must extract from it an infinite relative chain over $\mathrm{DP}_{\mathrm{rel}}(R,S)$.

**Why nontrivial / what must be proved:**
- Classical proof picks a *minimal* non-terminating term and follows root reductions. Here "minimal" must be w.r.t. $R/S$; define it and prove existence.
- Each marked $R$-step at the root produces the next pair; the interleaved $\to_S$ steps below the marked position must be absorbed into the chain's connection relation $\to_{R\cup S}^{*}$.
- **Key obstacle:** since $S$ need not terminate, $\to_S$ activity between two consecutive root-$R$-steps can be unbounded; show this does not obstruct the extraction (the connection relation tolerates arbitrarily long $\to_S^*$ segments).
- Handle that $\to_R$-steps may occur strictly below the marked position too; argue that infinitely many *root-level* marked $R$-steps can still be extracted (use minimality / pigeonhole).

Deliver a full proof, no "standard argument" shortcuts.
